purpose: Test whether two separately implemented adjudicators can classify previously unused boundary and composite bundles before expected outcomes enter the public Git history.

inputContract.canonicalDigestBoundary: RFC 8785 JCS for JSON values representable without non-finite numbers or duplicate object keys

outputContract.commitment: Each implementation publishes the RFC8785-JCS SHA-256 digest of its complete ordered prediction array before the reveal file is committed.
outputContract.comparison: After reveal, classify every mismatch as profile-ambiguity, parser-or-implementation-error, threat-model-disagreement, or reveal-error. An unexplained mismatch fails the cycle.

chronologyClaim.gitAnchor: A pushed pre-reveal commit proves only that the corpus and both output digests preceded the later reveal commit in this repository history.
chronologyClaim.trustedTime: Only a successfully verified RFC 3161 token over the committed payload digest may be described as trusted time. RC31 does not mint such a token.
chronologyClaim.transparency: A future append-only transparency service must provide inclusion and consistency evidence; a local digest file alone is not an external log.

packagePseudonymClaim.construction: An authorized enrollment service computes HMAC-SHA-256 with a study-specific secret over studyId, a custody-observed normalized package identifier, and a domain separator.
packagePseudonymClaim.use: Equality inside one study can expose duplicate packages and reruns without publishing the raw identifier.
packagePseudonymClaim.limits: The enrollment authority can still link records, key compromise removes dictionary resistance, and no digest proves that the observed object was a genuine package. Cross-study linkage is forbidden by key and study separation.

independenceBoundary.javascript: Reads the frozen corpus and implements schema and semantic decisions without importing Python code.
independenceBoundary.python: Reads the same frozen corpus and independently implements schema and semantic decisions without executing JavaScript.
independenceBoundary.remainingDependence: Both implementations are authored in one repository, use the same protocol text and corpus, and are not institutional or parser-library independent.

safety: All cases are synthetic documents. No production key, real package identifier, exploit, invasive measurement, vendor record, or live supply-chain action is included.
